prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states there, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my single-part position. After the full round-1 exchange the case still rests on one thing: a quantitative prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band condition at a specific twist angle) was tested seven years later and the predicted regime hosted correlated insulating and superconducting states, which many groups on many platforms have since reproduced. The discovery is one sentence long and has a single control parameter, which is what I mean by a discovery rather than a lifetime achievement. The three-name configuration is a natural prediction-plus-demonstration split and fits the three-person limit without a second part. The chair's observation that B009 was ranked by all eight members and placed in the top three by five is context only; I would hold this position on content if the counts were reversed. The citation should be worded around the flat bands and the observed phases, and should not claim that the pairing mechanism is understood.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection, which I take more seriously after round 1, is that the attribution is open on both sides and that the field is eight years old. On theory, Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto computed moire band structure earlier, and I cannot show from the supplied record that Bistritzer-MacDonald is uniquely decisive beyond the quantitative magic-angle condition. On experiment, Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby and others sit outside a three-name credit, and twist-angle disorder and strain mean the experimental record is less uniform than the theory. The pairing mechanism, the phase diagram and sample reproducibility are still debated. If a majority concludes that the committee should wait for a clearer picture, B049 is the more mature and more cleanly attributed alternative, although I still weigh its closeness to the 2005 and 2012 precision-measurement prizes.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that optical lattice clocks (B049) have a clean two-name credit, independent confirmation across laboratories and species, and a concrete route to redefining the second, and that waiting for the redefinition would reward administrative timing rather than the discovery.
responses.response: I accept the point about administrative timing and I will not make the redefinition of the second a condition for B049. The magic-wavelength idea is concrete and well confirmed. The question I cannot dismiss is whether it is a discovery or a decisive improvement in measurement, and you yourself note that the fundamental-physics results so far are null tests. That is why I still place B049 as my first alternative and not first. I also agree that we should apply one maturity standard to both candidates: B049 has two decades of confirmation, B009 has about eight years but a replicated phenomenon, and the unsettled item in B009 is the explanation of the superconductivity, not the existence of the states.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B049 and asks what would have to be established about distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and also notes that lattice-clock credit leaves out Lemonde, Ludlow and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups.
responses.response: On distinctness, a citation centred on the magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the light shift can be written so that it differs from the frequency comb and from ion control. That shifts my view somewhat, since I earlier weighed the lineage objection heavily. I do not think it removes the problem that the headline results are improved accuracy and null tests. I would not block a B049 award and I would accept it as the committee's choice if B009 cannot be settled, but I do not move it above B009. Your reservation about B009 being outside your specialty is honest and I do not read it as a scientific objection.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, moved from B026 to B049 and lists waiting for the redefinition of the second as an open uncertainty, and earlier raised the Lopes dos Santos priority question against B009.
responses.response: I still cannot resolve Lopes dos Santos from the record, so let me say how I would handle it. The decisive theory content is the quantitative magic-angle condition that was then tested, and the citation can say that without claiming that moire band structure began with Bistritzer and MacDonald. If that wording does not satisfy you, the committee could state the antecedent openly in the motivation. On your question of what the pairing mechanism has to establish: nothing, if the citation avoids it. A prize for a discovery does not require that its microscopic explanation be settled.

responses.point: Mehlig supports B009 with the same three names and argues that a Nobel discovery does not need a settled mechanism, and asks the others to consider colloidal-roller and vibrated-rod experiments for active matter (B011).
responses.response: I agree on the mechanism, with one difference of emphasis. Disorder and strain are not only a nuisance, so I would not say that the experimental record is uniform, and I would keep the citation limited to what is observed. On B011, I have looked at the argument and the colloidal-roller and rod experiments are suggestive, but no one has shown that they test the Toner-Tu exponents, and Yuhai Tu is outside the credit, as Johansson, Kroll and others say. I would not move it into the main discussion.

responses.point: Danielsson supports B009 but names maturity of interpretation as the main reason a committee might wait, and sees no combination that keeps a two-part prize within three people.
responses.response: I agree that a two-part configuration is not available: B009 alone uses all three names, and combining it with B049 would need five. That settles the shape for me, a single part. On maturity I differ slightly from you. I think the right test is whether the phenomenon has been reproduced and whether the credit can be defended, and on both counts B009 passes. The open interpretation is a reason to word the citation carefully, not a reason to wait. If you and I disagree here, the disagreement is about how large the risk is, not about the science.

responses.point: Johansson moved from B040 to B012 (Bloch, Greiner, Zoller) after the 2025 prize and the omission of Girvin and Devoret were raised, and argues that the Jaksch-Zoller proposal is what experiments implemented.
responses.response: I have kept B012 as an alternative and your argument for Zoller as the proposal behind the experiments is strong. My difficulty is that the configuration has four candidate names for three places, with Cirac also argued by Mehlig, and the topic sits near the 2001 and 2012 prizes. Eriksson ranked it seventh because the payoff of analogue simulation has not been shown, and I share that doubt. We are both at Chalmers; with B040 out of your preferred configuration that connection no longer bears on the choice between B009, B049 and B012.

uncertainties: Whether the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto antecedent should change the theory credit or only the wording of the citation.
Whether experimental credit should go to Jarillo-Herrero alone within the three-person limit, or whether Cao, Dean, Young or Yacoby have a claim that outweighs Bistritzer's.
Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder make eight years too early for a prize that must withstand later developments.
Whether B049 is a discovery or a precision-measurement advance, and whether a citation can be made clearly distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
I am relying on recollection of the credit history and the supplied record, and have not verified the claims independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with the B009 candidates (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) is documented in my profile, and I have no collaboration with them. My electron microscopy of oxide interfaces, including lanthanum-aluminate/strontium-titanate, is adjacent to but distinct from moire graphene. I share Chalmers with Johansson, which is a collegial connection, and since B040 is no longer in his preferred configuration it does not bear on the likely deciding candidates. No change in disclosure since round 1.
